newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mugabe flight engineers suspended, report.
newsitem.headline: Mugabe flight engineers suspended, report.

text.p: Engineers at Zimbabwe's state-owned airline were suspended on Tuesday for refusing to service a plane which carried President Robert Mugabe to a world food summit in Rome, state media reported.
The Zimbabwean news agency, ZIANA, said Air Zimbabwe had suspended 35 engineers over the issue.

Airline officials were unavailable for comment, but the Zimbabwe Aircraft Maintenance Engineers Association (ZAMEA) said some of its members only declined to work overtime and Air Zimbabwe management were victimising the engineers for a recent two-week go-slow for better salaries and working conditions.
"This is an attempt to thwart the current negotiations on their (engineers) demands," ZAMEA said in a statement.

Mugabe's trip to the World Food Summit on Monday night has already been marred by controversy, with a top trade union leader saying he should have stayed home to resolve a three- week strike by nurses and doctors which has paralysed Zimbabwe's public health sector.
